extraction.name: MATH Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems from high school math competitions, each with a full step-by-step solution and a final boxed answer. It is designed to measure mathematical problem-solving ability in machine learning models. The paper also introduces AMPS, a large auxiliary mathematics pretraining corpus.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Bums, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.citeAs: Hendrycks, Dan et al. Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset. NeurIPS 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MATH dataset consists of problems from mathematics competitions including AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more. Many problems can be collected from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests. Problems are curated from the competition mathematics community and include step-by-step solutions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Competition mathematics problems from AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and other mathematics competitions; many collected from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Problems and solutions are consistently formatted using LaTeX and Asymptote. Final answers are normalized with formatting rules so equivalent expressions are treated as the same during evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Final boxed answers are forced to follow consistent formatting rules; probabilities are expressed as simplified fractions; fractions, coefficients, variable ordering, parentheses, spaces, and equivalent numeric forms are normalized for exact-match evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem has a step-by-step solution and a final boxed answer. Problems are tagged by difficulty from 1 to 5 and span seven subjects.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Automatic assessment parses the answer inside the \boxed{} command and compares it to the ground truth answer while accounting for equivalent formatting. The paper also notes that step-by-step solutions can be incorrect or misleading even when the final answer is correct.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 step-by-step solution and 1 final boxed answer per problem
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors state they do not intend for the dataset to train models that help students cheat on mathematics exams, and instead intend it to be used to better forecast reasoning capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is drawn from high school mathematics competitions and thus reflects competition mathematics and the best young mathematical talent in the United States; it is not representative of all mathematics problems or all populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Accuracy remains relatively low even for large models; the dataset is challenging for both models and humans. It is intended for benchmarking mathematical reasoning rather than straightforward plug-and-chug tasks, and the authors do not intend it for helping students cheat on mathematics exams.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking/testing mathematical problem-solving ability; training and fine-tuning models on questions, answers, and step-by-step solutions; evaluating exact-match answer generation; forecasting reasoning capabilities.
